summary: Combined DM→Pinpoint observe-not-reupload wiring and fake release→import/content/search lifecycle fit the intended cross-module shape. The material risk is ExpectedOutput remaining a single unscoped array while DM and Pinpoint invent incompatible silent filters, with interface docs still describing the old fail/refuse semantics.

findings.summary: Shared expectedOutputs has no stage affinity; adapters silently drop different assertion types.
findings.rationale: One fixture array now drives three policies: DM verifyOutputPackage omits search-finds when deferSearchFinds (dm-release only); Pinpoint verifyRevision strips document-count before unverifiableOutputs; direct Pinpoint prepare still refuses document-count. Deferred/skipped rows vanish from that stage’s AssertionResult list rather than being recorded as skipped, so combined fixtures (e.g. s1kd-contract-pipeline) encode cross-product intent only in ad-hoc call-site filters. content-contains is also evaluated twice on the combined path (DM zip entries vs Pinpoint HTML refkeys) under the same schema type with different match rules. Without fixture- or schema-level stage scoping, the next workflow or assertion type will likely add a third filter rather than a shared contract.

findings.summary: Published LTF-004/005 and fake-surface docs still contradict the new split-verify contract.
findings.rationale: LTF-004 still states search-finds fails on DM with an explicit missing-phase detail, but dm-release now defers those rows. LTF-005 still lists document-count as refused before upload with no note that verifyRevision silently skips it for dm-publish-to-pinpoint. docs/load-testing-framework.md still claims Pinpoint content/search are not modelled and that content visibility can only be checked on real Pinpoint. The new mock section around the fake content/search routes was updated, so the shared interface docs now disagree with each other and with the adapters—classic data-contract drift for anyone wiring fixtures or reading LTF-004/005 as authority.
